clue.text: Dull backing among acacias or phloxes

indicators.note: backing tells us to read the run of concealed letters from right to left
among says the letters sit inside the run of words acacias or phloxes

explanation.surface: A dull garden border, with acacias and phloxes planted behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, the run ciasorp from acaCIAS OR Phloxes gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prosaic is ordinary and unimaginative, a synonym for dull.

clue.text: Italian bar worker taking lid off frothy coffees

indicators.note: taking ... off means removing the named piece
off completes taking off, removing the lid from the top

parts.note: cappuccini is the Italian plural of cappuccino, a frothy coffee
a cap is a lid

explanation.surface: An Italian barista takes the lid off some frothy coffees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar worker' looks like a barista but means a composer, who writes music in bars.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer of La Bohème and Tosca worked in musical bars, so he is an Italian composer.

clue.text: Wring 25 drops

indicators.note: wring means twist, so the letters of the other answer are twisted into a new order

parts.note: 25 points to the answer at 25 across, meaning not too dry

explanation.surface: Wring out something damp and drops fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to drop it, the verb sense, synonym of excluding.

clue.text: Key-ring?

parts.note: A is a musical key
to toll is to ring a bell

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the ring that holds your keys.
explanation.walkthrough: A key is a low coral island, and the answer is one shaped like a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon is a ring-like island, or cay.

clue.text: Retail group admitting gross humiliation

indicators.note: admitting means letting the other piece in

parts.note: a chain is a group of shops
GR is an abbreviation for gross, twelve dozen

explanation.surface: A shop chain confesses to gross humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexation or mortification at being disappointed is a sense close to humiliation.

clue.text: Was woozy pedestrian briefly stuck in Slough?

parts.note: when your head swam you felt giddy, so was woozy gives swam
the first three letters of pedestrian, cut short

explanation.surface: A dizzy walker, it seems, has got stuck in the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is a bog, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or mire, so being stuck in one is being bogged down, a cryptic definition by example.

clue.text: Demon on board resorts to raise (very high)

parts.note: spas are health resorts
to sky a ball is to hit it very high

explanation.surface: A devil aboard ship heads to resorts to raise hell.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Spassky was world chess champion 1969-72; the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A formidable chess player is a whizz at the game played on a board, here a former world champion.

clue.text: Governors in South Africa House go through the roof's attachment to floor

parts.note: the ANC is the ruling party of South Africa
to go through the roof is to rage in fury

explanation.surface: South Africa's governors at the House lose their temper over how the roof is fixed to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring place where a ship is held to the sea floor by its heavy iron hook.

clue.text: Perhaps bushy Scotsman's gear turns up when shaver comes round

indicators.note: comes round means the tool wraps itself around the other piece

parts.note: a plane is a carpenter's tool that shaves wood

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a kilt is traditional Scottish dress

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's kilt turns up when a razor comes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bushy is one example of resembling vegetation, hence the 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Level weight system follows regularly observed diets

indicators.note: follows puts the weight system after the selected letters
regularly observed picks every other letter of the word diets

parts.note: troy is the system of weights for precious metals

explanation.surface: A dieter's weigh-in that keeps things on an even level.
explanation.definitionFit: To level a building is to raze it to the ground, demolishing it utterly.

clue.text: Rose fruit in soft drink? I'm grateful for party snack

indicators.note: in says the fruit is placed inside the drink

parts.note: cola is a fizzy soft drink
a hip is the fruit of the rose
ta is informal British thanks

explanation.surface: Someone offered a rosehip cola thanks the host for the party nibbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail sausage served on sticks is a classic British party nibble.

clue.text: Omnishambles initially limited by Conservative is characterised by bedlam

indicators.note: limited by means hemmed in by the surrounding letters

parts.note: a thing that is characterised by a quality has it

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word Omnishambles

explanation.surface: A political commentator says a Tory omnishambles is pure bedlam.
explanation.walkthrough: Omnishambles was a 2012 coinage for a government in total disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, after the old London asylum, means total disorder and uproar.

clue.text: Slight cunning, always seeing Time Out as narrow-minded

indicators.note: always means each of the two words loses the letter, not just one
Out says the letter for Time is removed

parts.note: a slight is an insult
art can mean craft or cunning
T is the abbreviation for time, removed here from both words

explanation.surface: A bigot is accused of petty craftiness and of never taking time off.
explanation.walkthrough: Both INSULT and ART drop a T for 'Time Out', which 'always' extends to each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Island-minded people cut off from outside ideas are parochial and narrow in outlook.

clue.text: Small bike making a comeback, also in sports grounds

indicators.note: making a comeback means the whole assembly goes back to front
in places one word inside the other

parts.note: recs is short for recreation grounds, where games are played
too means also

explanation.surface: Small bikes return to the playing fields as a fashion revival.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor scooter is a light, small-wheeled motorcycle.

clue.text: Nuts need cynic's coarseness

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, telling us the letters go haywire into a new order

explanation.surface: Crazy people need a cynic's crude bluntness.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse, vulgar behaviour or language is described as lewd or improper conduct.

clue.text: Old violins which broken red cases render playable

indicators.note: cases means holds inside, like an instrument in its box
broken means the letters of red are rearranged

parts.note: Amatis are violins made by the Amati family of Cremona

explanation.surface: Old violins in red cases, though broken, are made playable again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges RED to DRE; 'render playable' means turn into a play, not tune an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt a story for the stage is to turn it into a play, so render it fit for performance.

clue.text: Doctor to palace seizing Republican for old queen

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing and holding the letter inside
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor called to the palace seizes a Republican plotting against the old queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The last Ptolemaic ruler of Egypt, lover of Antony, is a famous ancient monarch.

clue.text: Pacific state vanishes in disaster for friendship

indicators.note: vanishes in says the state's abbreviation drops out of the longer word

parts.note: a calamity is a disaster
Cal is an abbreviation for California, on the Pacific coast

explanation.surface: A West Coast state disappears in a catastrophe, ending a friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is peaceful goodwill between people or nations, a close synonym.

clue.text: Smooth shape of bolt sheathed by bar

indicators.note: sheathed by means wrapped inside the other word like a blade in a scabbard

parts.note: bar can mean except, as can save
a U-bolt is bent into the shape of the letter U

explanation.surface: A workshop description of a bolt slid smoothly into a metal bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth operator is polished and urbane in manner, a synonym.

clue.text: Look at holding search for Welsh tenor

indicators.note: holding means containing the other piece

parts.note: to see is to look at
to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: Talent scouts look into a search for a Welsh singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Harry Secombe was a Welsh tenor and comedian, one of the Goons.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Secombe, the Goon Show comic, was also a celebrated Welsh singer.

clue.text: Witch's word introducing alternative female deity among saints

indicators.note: among says the other pieces go between the two saint letters

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for saint, so two saints give SS
or is the word that introduces an alternative
Ceres is the Roman goddess of agriculture

explanation.surface: A witch's spell offers a choice of goddess to be placed among the saints.
explanation.definitionFit: A female practitioner of magic is the woman's counterpart of a sorcerer, a synonym.

clue.text: Singular Dickensian clerk loses it in nick

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: loses means the following word is dropped

parts.note: Bob Cratchit is Scrooge's clerk in A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: A unique Dickensian clerk loses his temper in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' looks like British slang for prison, but it is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cut or graze on the skin is a minor nick.

clue.text: Batman's adversary toppled Lord protected by horseman

indicators.note: protected by means held inside the other word

parts.note: a rider is a horseman

indicators.note: toppled in a down clue means turned upside down, read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A lord knocked down and shielded by a horseman, like a scene from Gotham.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle-setting villain in green is one of Batman's foes.

clue.text: Stone contains little that is precious

indicators.note: contains means the abbreviation holds the next piece

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A tiny precious stone is set in a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious used as a fond address, like darling, is a term of endearment for a loved one.

clue.text: Someone reserved parking; I'm doubtful he'll stop moving vehicles

parts.note: a clam is a reticent person who says little
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
er is a hesitant noise of doubt

explanation.surface: A driver who booked a space hesitates, unsure whether the warden will tow the cars.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, wardens fit wheel clamps to illegally parked cars so they cannot be driven off.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who fixes immobilising locks to car wheels prevents those vehicles moving.

clue.text: Parisian from Tours gets placed in rowing

indicators.note: in says the second phrase sits inside the French word

parts.note: de is French for from, and Tours is a French city
is put means gets placed

explanation.surface: A Parisian travelling from Tours finds himself in a rowing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rowing' suggests oars, but here a row is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing in the sense of quarrelling noisily is an argument or a disagreement.

clue.text: Avid supporter in America raised 10 there

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means turned upward, read from the bottom
in places the supporter inside the country's letters

parts.note: US is America
a fan is an avid supporter

explanation.surface: An avid supporter in America stirred up bedlam over there.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is the answer at 10 across, meaning bedlam; 'there' points back to America.
explanation.definitionFit: This US military acronym means a situation of total muddle, used as American slang.

clue.text: Let me see Gaultier's pal with good taste

parts.note: um is a thinking noise, like let me see
ami is French for friend, Jean Paul Gaultier being a French designer

explanation.surface: A fashion designer's friend with good taste is introduced hesitantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth basic flavour, a savoury richness, is a pleasant taste.

clue.text: Red, not counting last of Rioja, is not too dry

indicators.note: not counting means leaving out the letter named

parts.note: a Maoist is a communist, a red

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word Rioja

explanation.surface: A red wine, discounting the Rioja, is said to be not too dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly damp is the sense: moderately wet, the opposite of parched.

clue.text: Pick out unfinished carrying surface, the kind fork-lifts take back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the combined pieces from end to start
unfinished drops the final letter

parts.note: a tray is a flat surface for carrying things
a pallet is the wooden platform a fork-lift truck lifts

explanation.surface: Instructions for choosing the right platform for a fork-lift truck to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole of TRA plus PALLET.
explanation.definitionFit: To distinguish one thing from another is to pick it out from the rest.

clue.text: Hospital sell-off you once rejected as part of small fringe

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the assembly is read in reverse

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
a sale is a sell-off
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A hospital sale is turned down as merely a small fringe event.
explanation.definitionFit: The fringe of hairs on an eyelid is made up of many of these, each one a single hair.

clue.text: Set of instructions concerned with keeping public at home

indicators.note: keeping means holding the other pieces within

parts.note: re means about or concerning
something out is public knowledge
in means at home

explanation.surface: Guidance about keeping the public at home.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, a subprogram that performs a task is a sequence of coded commands.
